title: Getting to North Sikkim: Gangtok, Permits and the Road
meta_description: How to reach Lachung, Lachen, Mangan and Dzongu: NJP to Gangtok on NH10, the permit day, Vajra taxi stand jeeps, and the road since the 2023 Teesta flood.
summary: All trips to North Sikkim start in Gangtok. Reach it from NJP or Bagdogra by shared jeep on NH10 in 4–5 hours, spend a day getting your permit through a registered agent, then leave by tour vehicle or shared jeep from Vajra taxi stand. Roads have closed often since October 2023; check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Step one: reach Gangtok
paras: The nearest railway station is New Jalpaiguri (NJP) and the nearest major airport is Bagdogra, both on the edge of Siliguri in West Bengal. From either, shared jeeps leave for Gangtok through the day from the Sikkim Nationalised Transport (SNT) stand and the Panitanki area in Siliguri, and from outside NJP. A seat costs about ₹300–450 and the drive takes 4–5 hours on NH10, the highway that follows the Teesta from Sevoke up through Rangpo, where you enter Sikkim, to Singtam and Gangtok. A reserved car costs ₹3,500–4,500.

NH10 is the lifeline of Sikkim and also its weakest link. The October 2023 Teesta flood washed out sections of it, and since then stretches near Teesta Bazar, Melli and Rangpo have collapsed or closed repeatedly, especially in the monsoon. When NH10 is shut, vehicles take the longer route through Lava, Algarah and Pedong on the Kalimpong side, NH717A, which adds two to four hours. Pakyong airport, about 30 km from Gangtok, has had only patchy flights. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Step two: the permit day in Gangtok
paras: Give yourself at least one full day in Gangtok before going north. Indian nationals need a North Sikkim permit for Lachung, Yumthang, Zero Point, Lachen, Thangu, Chopta and Gurudongmar, and only registered tour operators can apply for it. Go to an agent on or near MG Marg in the morning with a copy of a government photo ID (Aadhaar, voter ID, passport or driving licence) and two passport photographs per person. The agent files the application, and the permit is usually ready for a departure the next morning.

Foreign nationals need a Protected Area Permit, applied for through a registered agent, for a group of two or more. They have usually been allowed to Lachung and Yumthang but not to Zero Point or Gurudongmar. Dzongu needs a separate permit, usually issued in Mangan. The day also helps your body adjust at Gangtok's 1,650 m before you climb to 2,700 m and above. Rules and permitted points change: check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Vajra taxi stand and the shared jeeps
paras: Vajra taxi stand, about 3 km north of the Gangtok centre on the North Sikkim road, is where the jeeps for the north start. From here shared jeeps run through the day to Kabi, Phodong, Mangan, Singhik and Chungthang, and many North Sikkim tour vehicles assemble here around 10–11 am once permits are in hand. A local taxi from MG Marg to Vajra costs ₹150–250.

For places that need no permit for Indians, Vajra is all you need. Buy a seat at the counter, load your bag on the roof, and you are in Kabi Lungchok in under an hour or Mangan in about three. Shared jeeps to Lachung and Chungthang carry local people, but visitors still need the permit, and in practice that means a tour.

sections.heading: The road north, stage by stage
paras: The North Sikkim road leaves Gangtok past Vajra, climbs over a shoulder to Kabi and Phodong, then drops into the Teesta gorge. Past Mangan and Singhik it runs through Toong to Chungthang, the river town at about 1,790 m where the Lachen Chu and Lachung Chu meet. Tour vehicles stop at roadside waterfalls such as Seven Sisters and Naga falls for tea and photos.

At Chungthang the road forks: left up the Lachen Chu to Lachen, right up the Lachung Chu to Lachung. Police and army check posts along the way inspect permits, so keep your copy where you can reach it. The drive to either village takes 6–8 hours in good conditions. After the flood, the crossing at Chungthang and the road to Lachen have been the slowest to recover, and diversions, single-lane stretches and night closures are common.

sections.heading: The road situation since 2023
paras: On the night of 3–4 October 2023 the South Lhonak glacial lake burst, and the Teesta flood destroyed the Teesta III dam at Chungthang and long stretches of road and several bridges down the valley. North Sikkim was cut off for weeks. Since then it has reopened in stages: Lachung and Yumthang have generally been open more often than Lachen and Gurudongmar, which have stayed closed for long spells. Monsoon landslides in 2024 and 2025 stranded travellers in the high villages again.

Here is how we handle it: decide nothing until you are in Gangtok, ask two agents what is open that week, read the Mangan district administration's and Sikkim Police's latest notices, and keep at least one buffer day at the end of the trip. Check current status before you travel, and again the evening before you leave.
list: Keep a buffer day between your return to Gangtok and any train or flight from NJP or Bagdogra.
Carry cash for two extra days in case a road closes behind you.
Keep printed and phone copies of your permit and photo ID.
Download offline maps; signal fails for long stretches beyond Mangan.

sections.heading: A sample plan from the plains
paras: Here is the timeline we suggest for a first North Sikkim trip from NJP or Bagdogra, with one buffer day built in. It assumes the 3-day, 2-night shared tour; add nights for Dzongu, Singhik or a slower Lachung stay.

The buffer day is not wasted. If the north road closes while you are up there, it absorbs the delay; if all goes well, spend it at Kabi Lungchok and Phodong by shared jeep from Vajra, or at Rumtek and Gangtok's monasteries. Never book a train or flight from NJP or Bagdogra for the same day you come down from Lachung.
list: Day 1: shared jeep or car from NJP or Bagdogra to Gangtok, 4–5 hours on NH10, longer via Lava and Pedong if NH10 is shut. Visit agents in the evening if you arrive early.
Day 2: book the tour and hand in ID copies and photographs in the morning. Rest, walk MG Marg, eat early.
Day 3: depart around 10–11 am from Vajra stand or the agent's office; reach Lachen by evening.
Day 4: Gurudongmar at dawn, then on to Lachung.
Day 5: Yumthang, and Zero Point if open, then back to Gangtok by night.
Day 7: back down to NJP or Bagdogra.

sections.heading: Getting to Dzongu and Mangan
paras: Dzongu is the one part of North Sikkim where independent travel works well. Take a shared jeep from Vajra to Mangan, get or collect your Dzongu permit there, then take a taxi across the Teesta to your homestay village for ₹800–1,500, depending on distance and how the bridges are. Many homestays arrange both the permit and the pickup if you send ID copies ahead. A reserved car from Gangtok straight to a Dzongu village costs about ₹3,500–5,000 one way.

faqs.q: How do I get from NJP to North Sikkim?
faqs.a: Go to Gangtok first. Shared jeeps from NJP and Siliguri's SNT stand cost ₹300–450 a seat and take 4–5 hours on NH10; a reserved car costs ₹3,500–4,500. Spend a day in Gangtok while an agent gets your permit, then leave for Lachung or Lachen by tour vehicle. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Where is Vajra taxi stand in Gangtok?
faqs.a: About 3 km north of the town centre, on the road toward North Sikkim. Shared jeeps leave from here for Kabi, Phodong, Mangan, Singhik and Chungthang, and many North Sikkim tour vehicles gather here around 10–11 am. A local taxi from MG Marg costs about ₹150–250.

faqs.q: Can I get a North Sikkim permit on the same day?
faqs.a: Rarely. Agents usually need a day to file and collect the permit, so most people book one day and leave the next morning. Arrive in Gangtok with ID copies and two photographs per person to avoid delays. In peak weeks, apply as soon as you arrive. Check current status before you travel.

It changes often. Since the October 2023 Teesta flood, sections of NH10 near Teesta Bazar, Melli and Rangpo have collapsed or closed repeatedly, especially in the monsoon. When it shuts, vehicles take the longer route via Lava and Pedong, NH717A, adding two to four hours. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is the road to Lachen open?
faqs.a: Not always. The Lachen road and the Chungthang crossing have been the slowest parts of North Sikkim to recover from the 2023 flood, and have closed for long spells, while Lachung often stayed open. Ask two Gangtok agents that week, read the Mangan district notices, and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How long is the drive from Gangtok to Lachung?
faqs.a: About 118 km and 6–8 hours in good conditions, with tea stops at waterfalls and lunch near Mangan or Chungthang. Lachen is about 129 km and takes as long. Landslide repairs, diversions and check posts can add hours, so tours leave Gangtok by 11 am and arrive around dusk.

faqs.q: Can I drive my own car to North Sikkim?
faqs.a: Generally no, for the high valleys. Permits are issued through registered tour operators, and vehicles from outside Sikkim are usually not allowed to Lachung, Lachen and the points above them. You can drive to Kabi, Phodong and Mangan. Rules change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How do I get to Dzongu from Gangtok?
faqs.a: Take a shared jeep from Vajra stand to Mangan for ₹200–300, about 3 hours. Get your Dzongu permit in Mangan, then take a taxi to your village for ₹800–1,500. Many homestays arrange both if you send ID copies ahead. A reserved car from Gangtok costs ₹3,500–5,000 one way.

faqs.q: Is there a flight to Gangtok?
faqs.a: Pakyong airport, about 30 km from Gangtok, has had only patchy commercial flights since it opened, with long gaps. Most travellers fly to Bagdogra and take a jeep or car up, 4–5 hours by NH10. Check the current flight schedule and road status before you travel.
